info.title: Luma API
info.description:
API for interacting with Luma's event platform.

## Rate Limits

The Luma API uses a per-minute rate limit shared across `GET` and `POST` requests:

- **Calendar API keys** and OAuth tokens: **200 requests/minute** per calendar.
- **Organization API keys**: **500 requests/minute** per organization.

When you exceed the limit the API returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Back off before retrying.

get.description:
Every event and API key on Luma is managed by a [Luma Calendar](https://help.luma.com/p/luma-calendar-overview). By default this lists the events your Calendar manages.

Each event includes an `access` field. Pass `access=manage&access=view` to also return events that are listed on the Calendar but managed elsewhere — those come back with `access: "view"`, their location obfuscated to city level, and host-only fields like `meeting_url`, `registration_questions`, and `feedback_email` omitted. Private events the Calendar doesn't manage are never returned.

get.description: List all events across all calendars belonging to the organization. Events are deduplicated if they appear on multiple calendars within the organization.

coordinate.description: Latitude and longitude of the event location. Null for online events or when the address can't be geocoded.

location_type.description: `offline` for in-person events. Online events have the meeting platform (`zoom`, `meet`, etc.), or `unknown` if we don't recognize the meeting link. `missing` if the event has no location set.

location_visibility.description: Whether the event's address is shown to everyone or only to approved guests. Events you manage always return the full address.

waitlist_status.description: `enabled` if the event has a waitlist. New registrations join the waitlist once the event reaches capacity.

registration_open.description: Whether the host is accepting registrations. When `false`, registration is closed and new guests can't sign up. Independent of capacity — a sold-out event with `waitlist_status` disabled still reports `true`.

require_approval.description: `true` if registering requires host approval — i.e. any currently available ticket has approval turned on.

max_capacity.description: The maximum number of approved tickets allowed across all ticket types, as configured by the host. Null when the event has no capacity limit (individual ticket types may still be capped). `spots_remaining` reports how many are left.

can_register_for_multiple_tickets.description: Whether a guest can register for multiple tickets in one registration (Group Registration). When `true`, each ticket counts toward `max_capacity`.

spots_remaining.description: Spots left before the event hits its max capacity. Null when the event has no capacity limit (even if individual ticket types are capped). Refreshed by a background job, so this can lag a few seconds behind registrations.

amount.description: Starting (lowest) ticket price in the currency's minor unit (e.g. cents for USD), tax included.

is_flexible.description: `true` for pay-what-you-want pricing — `amount` is the suggested price and guests can pay more.

display_price.description: The starting ticket price shown on the event card. Null when registration is free — or, rarely, when nothing is currently purchasable (e.g. all paid tickets have expired). Refreshed by a background job, so this can lag a few seconds behind ticket changes.

enabled.description: Whether to send the feedback email.

delay.description: How long after the event ends to send the feedback email. Defaults to PT0M (immediately). Maximum is P30D. A negative duration (e.g. -PT30M) sends it before the event ends — at most P1D before, and never before the event starts.

feedback_email.description: Settings for the post-event feedback email sent to guests.

zoom_meeting_url.description: Use `meeting_url` instead. Not all meetings use Zoom.

launch_status.description: Calendar status: launched means Active; coming-soon shows a placeholder page; archived stops new follows and visitor event submissions.

anyOf.description: A hex color like '#bb2dc7'. Shorthand (#rgb) is expanded and alpha channels (#rgba, #rrggbbaa) are stripped.

region.description: State or province, e.g. 'New York' or 'California'.

country.description: Country name, e.g. 'United States'. Null for cities in disputed territories where Google omits the country.

timezone.description: IANA timezone of the city, e.g. 'America/New_York'.

location.description: City the calendar is based in (e.g. for city calendars). Null when the calendar isn't tied to a place.

coordinate.description: Latitude and longitude of the calendar's primary location (e.g. city calendars). Null when the calendar isn't tied to a place.

status.description: Status of the event on this calendar.

managing_calendars.description: Calendars with manage access to this event, with the event's status on each. Calendars that only list the event without manage access are not included.

event_id.description: Event ID, this usually starts with evt-

suppress_email.description: If true, Luma will not email guests when updating the event name, time, or location. Guests still get a push notification for a changed time or location.

tax_config.description: Tax added on top of ticket prices for this event only, overriding the calendar’s tax setting. Pass `null` to go back to the calendar’s setting. Requires Luma Pro on the event’s calendar. Only affects new purchases.

confirmation_email_md.description: Your message in the confirmation email, sent when a registration is confirmed, including when you approve a guest. Supports Markdown formatting. Leave this field out to keep the current message or use the default email for a new event. To remove your message, use an empty string (`""`). Guests will still receive the standard email.

pending_approval_email_md.description: Your message in the email sent to guests awaiting approval or joining the waitlist. Supports Markdown formatting. Leave this field out to keep the current message or use the default email for a new event. To remove your message, use an empty string (`""`). Guests will still receive the standard email.

declined_email_md.description: Your message in the email sent when you decline a guest's registration. Supports Markdown formatting. Leave this field out to keep the current message or use the default email for a new event. To remove your message, use an empty string (`""`). Guests will still receive the standard email.

can_register_for_multiple_tickets.description: Whether a guest can register for multiple tickets in one registration (Group Registration). When `true`, each ticket counts toward `max_capacity`.

cover_url.description: Specify an image that has been uploaded to the Luma CDN. You can upload an image after getting an upload URL from the Luma API, or pick one from Luma’s cover gallery with `/v1/images/search`.

create_meeting.description: Create a new Zoom meeting or Google Meet with the Zoom or Google account the user has connected to Luma, and use its join link as the event's `meeting_url`. Fails if that account isn't connected. On update, replaces the current link; only the event's creator can create a Zoom meeting. Can't be combined with `meeting_url` or `geo_address_json`.

description_md.description: Format your text with Markdown. For images, request an upload URL from `/v1/images/create-upload-url`, upload the image, and use the returned `file_url` in `![alt](url)`. Image URLs must be hosted on images.lumacdn.com. To embed a YouTube, Vimeo, or Loom video, put its URL on a line of its own. Embedded Luma event cards aren't supported.

font.description: Font for the event name and headings on the event page. Setting a `theme` without a `font` applies the theme’s default font; pass `null` to clear the font and use the standard font. Fonts may be retired over time — a retired font stops being accepted here, and event pages still using one fall back to the standard font.

geo_address_json.description: In-person location. Use `{ type: 'manual', address }` with a free-text address, `{ type: 'google', place_id }` with a Google Places ID, or `{ type: 'lookup', query }` to search Google Maps and use the top result. Leave out for online events.

oneOf.description: Stores the address text as-is, without geocoding.

description.description: Extra directions shown alongside the address, e.g. "Suite 36" or "Enter through the side door".

oneOf.description: Resolves a Google Maps Place ID into a full address.

description.description: Extra directions shown alongside the address, e.g. "Suite 36" or "Enter through the side door".

oneOf.description: Searches Google Maps for `query` and uses the top result. If nothing matches, the query is stored as a manual address.

location_visibility.description: Set to `guests-only` to hide the precise location from people who haven't been approved — they'll see only the city and approximate area. Defaults to `public`.

max_capacity.description:
Once an event hits the max capacity, the event will be marked as sold out and registration will automatically be closed.

If the event has a waitlist (`waitlist_status` is `enabled`), new registrations join the waitlist instead of being closed.

If `can_register_for_multiple_tickets` is `true`, each ticket will count towards the max capacity.

meeting_url.description: Join link for online events (Zoom, Google Meet, etc.). To have Luma create one, use `create_meeting` instead. Can't be combined with `geo_address_json`.

name_requirement.description: How to collect guest names: `full-name` uses a single field; `first-last` uses separate first and last name fields. Enabling `first-last` requires Luma Plus on the event's calendar.

registration_open.description: Whether to accept registrations. Set to `false` to close registration so new guests can't sign up. Defaults to `true`.

reminders_disabled.description: By default, Luma will send reminders before the event. Turn off if you'd like more control over event communications.

feedback_email.description: Settings for the post-event feedback email sent to guests. If not specified on create, inherits from calendar defaults.

enabled.description: Whether to send the feedback email.

delay.description: How long after the event ends to send the feedback email. Defaults to PT0M (immediately). Maximum is P30D. A negative duration (e.g. -PT30M) sends it before the event ends — at most P1D before, and never before the event starts.

show_guest_list.description: When the guest list is shown, approved guests will be able to see who else is going to the event.

slug.description:
The URL slug for the event. If the slug is `aloha`, the URL will be `https://luma.com/aloha`. If the slug is not available, the event creation will fail.

You can use `/v1/entities/lookup` to check if a slug is available.

theme.description: Theme for the event page. Themes may be retired over time — a retired theme stops being accepted here, and event pages still using one fall back to `standard`. Setting a theme also applies the theme’s default font unless you pass `font`.

tint_color.description: Accent color for the event page, as a 3 or 6-digit hex code like `#bb2dc7`. We adjust the shade as needed so text and buttons stay accessible against the background.

waitlist_status.description: `enabled` if the event has a waitlist. New registrations join the waitlist once the event reaches capacity.

schema.description: Empty response

post.description: Update a guest’s status. Set `status` to `approved` ("Going"), `declined`, `pending_approval`, or `waitlist`. Use `should_refund` to refund a paid guest when moving them out of an approved state. Use `message` to include a personal note in the email we send the guest. To send a soft invite that guests can accept, use `/v1/events/guests/send-invites` instead.

event_id.description: Event ID, this usually starts with evt-

guest_id.description: Guest identifier — the guest ID (gst-), a ticket key, a guest key (g-), or the user's email.

should_refund.description: If you are moving a guest who has paid to `declined`, `waitlist`, or `pending_approval`, should we refund their payment? Defaults to false.

send_email.description: Optional. Whether Luma should email the guest about the status change. Defaults to true. Set to false if your integration sends its own notifications.

message.description: Optional. Personal message included in the email we send the guest about the status change. Max of 200 characters. Can't be combined with `send_email: false`.

schema.description: Empty response

post.description: Add or remove tickets from an existing guest. Added tickets are complimentary. Removed tickets are invalidated and, if `should_refund` is set, refunded for what the guest paid for them; otherwise no money moves. You can’t change tickets for guests with pending payment holds. Administrative ticket changes can exceed event or ticket-type capacity.

event_id.description: Event ID, this usually starts with evt-

guest_id.description: Guest identifier — the guest ID (gst-), a ticket key, a guest key (g-), or the user's email.

ticket_ids_to_remove.description: Existing ticket IDs to invalidate. At least one valid ticket must remain on the guest. Pass `should_refund` to refund the removed tickets.

items.description: Ticket ID, this usually starts with tkt-

should_refund.description: Optional. Refund each removed paid ticket for what the guest paid for it. The guest stays registered with their remaining tickets. The refund is limited to what's left on the order beyond the tickets the guest keeps, so a partial refund already issued from the dashboard isn't paid out again. Crypto payments can't be refunded this way. Defaults to false.

tickets_to_add.description: Complimentary tickets to grant. Each entry creates a new $0 administrative ticket, even when the ticket type is normally paid.

event_ticket_type_id.description: Ticket type ID, this usually starts with ttype-

send_email.description: Optional. Whether Luma may email the guest about the ticket change, including the refund receipt when `should_refund` is set. Defaults to true and still respects their notification preferences. This only controls email — the guest still gets an in-app notification, and push follows their preferences.

event_ticket_order_id.description: The ticket order the refund was issued against.

amount.description: The amount refunded, in minor units of `currency`.

refunds.description: Refunds issued for the removed tickets, one per ticket order. Empty unless `should_refund` was set.

post.description: Send guests an invite to an event. We'll send an email, and if their phone number is linked to their Luma account, they'll also receive an SMS. Invites are sent in the background; the response lists any guests that will be skipped because they unsubscribed from your calendar, were removed by an admin, or blocked you.

event_id.description: Event ID, this usually starts with evt-

guests.description: Information about the guests you want to invite to the event. If a user already has a name, this will not overwrite their name.

message.description: Personalize the message that will be included in the invite. Max of 200 characters.

skipped.description: Guests that won't be added because they unsubscribed from your calendar, were removed or blocked by a calendar admin, or there is a block between you and them. Everyone else in the request is processed.

post.description: Add guests to the event. By default, guests are added with the status "Going" (approved) and receive one ticket of the default ticket type. Use the `ticket` or `tickets` parameter to specify custom ticket assignments. Get available ticket types using `/v1/events/ticket-types/list`. Use `approval_status` to add guests as pending approval or on the waitlist instead of immediately approved. Use `registration_answers` on each guest to record answers to the event's registration questions — question IDs come from the `registration_questions` field of Get Event. Guests are added in the background; the response lists any guests that will be skipped because they unsubscribed from your calendar, were removed by an admin, or blocked you.

event_id.description: Event ID, this usually starts with evt-

registration_answers.description: Optional. The guest's answers to the event's registration questions. If the guest is already registered with answers, their existing answers are kept.

items.description: Information about the guests you want to add to the event. If a user already has a name, this will not overwrite their name.

ticket.description: Optional. Assign a single ticket of the specified type to each guest. Cannot be used with `tickets` parameter.

tickets.description: Optional. Assign multiple tickets to each guest. Each guest receives all tickets in the array. Use this to add multiple tickets of the same or different types. Cannot be used with `ticket` parameter.

approval_status.description: Optional. Status to assign to each added guest. Defaults to `approved` ("Going"). Use `pending_approval` to add guests for host review, or `waitlist` to add to the event waitlist. To send a soft invite that guests can accept, use `/v1/events/guests/send-invites` instead.

send_email.description: Optional. Whether Luma should email each added guest. Defaults to true. Set to false if your integration sends its own notifications.

skipped.description: Guests that won't be added because they unsubscribed from your calendar, were removed or blocked by a calendar admin, or there is a block between you and them. Everyone else in the request is processed.

post.description: Add a host to an event. This works for both managers and check-in staff — use the access_level parameter to control permissions.

event_id.description: Event ID, this usually starts with evt-

is_visible.description: Whether the host is shown on the event page. Defaults to true, except for `check-in` hosts, which are never shown — passing `true` with `check-in` is an error.

name.description: Name of the host you are adding. If they already have a Luma profile, this will be ignored.

schema.description: Empty response

post.description: Update a host's permissions or visibility on an event. Use this to change a host between check-in and manager access levels. The event creator's access level cannot be changed.

event_id.description: Event ID, this usually starts with evt-

email.description: Email of the host to update.

access_level.description: The new access level for the host. One of "none", "check-in", or "manager". The event creator’s access level cannot be changed.

is_visible.description: Whether the host is shown on the event page. `check-in` hosts are never shown: changing a host to `check-in` hides them, and passing `true` with `check-in` is an error.

schema.description: Empty response

post.description: Remove a host from an event. The event creator cannot be removed.

event_id.description: Event ID, this usually starts with evt-

email.description: Email of the host to remove.

schema.description: Empty response

post.description: Create a coupon that can be applied when a guest is registering for an event. Restrict it to a ticket type with `event_ticket_type_id` — when that ticket type is hidden, this creates an unlock (access) code. You are not able to edit the coupon terms after it has been created.

code.description: This is the code that the user will enter on the event page. It is not case sensitive. Maximum 20 characters.

remaining_count.description: Number of times the coupon can be used. Set to 1000000 for unlimited uses.

event_id.description: Event ID, this usually starts with evt-

event_ticket_type_id.description: Optional. Restrict the coupon to a single ticket type. If that ticket type is hidden, the coupon acts as an unlock (access) code that reveals the ticket during registration. Pair a hidden ticket type that has Require Approval turned off with an unlock code to let invited guests register and pay directly, skipping the Apply to Attend step. For a code that unlocks the ticket without changing the price, set the discount to 0% (`percent_off: 0`).

waitlist_status.description: `enabled` if the event has a waitlist. New registrations join the waitlist once the event reaches capacity.

registration_open.description: Whether the host is accepting registrations. When `false`, registration is closed and new guests can't sign up. Independent of capacity — a sold-out event with `waitlist_status` disabled still reports `true`.

require_approval.description: `true` if registering requires host approval — i.e. any currently available ticket has approval turned on.

max_capacity.description: The maximum number of approved tickets allowed across all ticket types, as configured by the host. Null when the event has no capacity limit (individual ticket types may still be capped). `spots_remaining` reports how many are left.

can_register_for_multiple_tickets.description: Whether a guest can register for multiple tickets in one registration (Group Registration). When `true`, each ticket counts toward `max_capacity`.

spots_remaining.description: Spots left before the event hits its max capacity. Null when the event has no capacity limit (even if individual ticket types are capped). Refreshed by a background job, so this can lag a few seconds behind registrations.

amount.description: Starting (lowest) ticket price in the currency's minor unit (e.g. cents for USD), tax included.

is_flexible.description: `true` for pay-what-you-want pricing — `amount` is the suggested price and guests can pay more.

display_price.description: The starting ticket price shown on the event card. Null when registration is free — or, rarely, when nothing is currently purchasable (e.g. all paid tickets have expired). Refreshed by a background job, so this can lag a few seconds behind ticket changes.

enabled.description: Whether to send the feedback email.

delay.description: How long after the event ends to send the feedback email. Defaults to PT0M (immediately). Maximum is P30D. A negative duration (e.g. -PT30M) sends it before the event ends — at most P1D before, and never before the event starts.

feedback_email.description: Settings for the post-event feedback email sent to guests.
